newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - APIs seen showing minor distillate build.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - APIs seen showing minor distillate build.

text.p: Despite frigid weather in the U.S. Northeast last week, the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected to report a slight build in distillate stocks in its oil inventory data expected Tuesday evening.

"Distillate supplies will likely show a slight increase with recent output hikes more than offsetting last week's relatively cold temperature patterns," said Jim Ritterbusch, trader with Sweeney Oil. A Reuters survey of trader and analyst forecasts shows a distillate stock build of 700,000 barrels for the data covering the week ended November 22.

Distillate output, which includes heating oil and diesel, is expected to remain near last week's feverish 3.6 million barrels a day. Total refinery utilization rates were seen rising almost 0.5 percentage point from 92.9 percent a week earlier as refineries continue to emerge from seasonal maintenance that began in autumn.
Crude stocks were seen unchanged to up two million barrels, tracking a historical pattern of builds at this time, traders said.
They said gasoline stocks could build one to three million barrels due to imports from Europe.

Distillate stock forecasts ranged from a draw of 300,000 barrels to a build of two million barrels. Last week's distillate stocks should not reflect higher heating oil demand due to below normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast since heating oil retailers stocked up in advance, analysts and traders said.

"The movement from primary to secondary storage happens way in advance of the cold weather," said John Saucer, an analyst with Smith Barney in Houston. Distillate output has remained high to replenish stocks that are running at a 15 million barrel deficit below a year ago.

Distillate stocks have built 3.3 million barrels in the past month. Some analysts said there could be a large build seen in this week's or next week's inventory data which would represent that last major distillate build for the winter season.
"We usually see a peak in (distillate) stocks this week or the first week in December. After that, there are declines," said A.G. Edwards analyst Bill O'Grady.
